dedupe_keys.name: ptna public transport network analysis for openstreetmap

description: PTNA (Public Transport Network Analysis) is an open-source quality-assurance system for public transport routes mapped in OpenStreetMap. Every day it analyses route and route_master relations, aggregates them per network and area, and compares them with target lists of lines supplied as CSV, flagging missing routes and errors such as gaps in itineraries; it also aggregates GTFS feeds and displays them in a readable way with shapes on a map, so mappers and analysts can compare the OSM network with the operator's timetable data. It was created and is maintained by the OpenStreetMap contributor ToniE and runs at ptna.openstreetmap.de. Coverage: the networks and areas configured on the site, across several countries; the wiki page does not list them. Access: website with an overview page, daily results and on-demand analysis. Licence and cost: GNU GPL for the software, free; OSM data are ODbL. Caveats: it focuses on the PTv2 tagging scheme and only checks what mappers and target lists provide, so a clean report does not prove the network is complete. It helps prepare verified transit network topology for network flow models and transit digital twins, and links OpenStreetMap to the GTFS feeds described by the GTFS specification record.
